subject: Post-demo: Cerebro performance recap & next-step plan
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@cerebrohealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-17T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: Cerebro performance recap & next-step plan

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the product demo earlier — appreciated the thoughtful questions from the AI/Ops team. As promised, I wanted to capture the performance items we covered and propose a short MAP (mutual action plan) so we can validate fit on SLOs and move toward procurement if everything aligns.

Summary of performance targets called out during the demo (please confirm):
- Latency goal: p95 <= 300 ms for short (<=128-token) chat responses; p95 <= 500 ms for long-form generation (~1k tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained throughput equivalent to ~600 tokens/sec across the cluster during daytime peak.
- Concurrency: support for 40 concurrent active user sessions with median interleaving of 8 requests/sec per session.
- Streaming requirements: token streaming with first-byte latency < 120 ms and delta token flushes <= 200 ms.
- Availability: 99.9% runtime SLA target; automatic fallback to smaller model variant during spikes.

Attachments: I’ve included a draft SLO checklist and the demo recording for your team to reference (see attachments).

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Performance validation run — Redwood to run baseline tests using Cerebro sample prompts (T+3 business days).
2) Scale canary — 48–72 hour canary with production-like traffic (customer provides traffic shape; Redwood provides canary config).
3) Pricing & contract — Redwood to provide a dedicated capacity quote and SLO language (T+5 business days).
4) Security / SOC2 evidence request — Redwood to share SOC2 report + pen test summary; Cerebro to provide any additional compliance checklist items.

Action items for you: please confirm the SLO numbers above (latency/throughput/concurrency/streaming), and share a sample traffic profile or representative prompt set so we can schedule the validation run. Also please confirm the procurement contact for contract routing.

I’ll coordinate the internal owners — Monica will lead the canary setup; Neha will own the performance validations and instrumentation hooks.

Best,

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: 20260217-slo-checklist.xlsx (SLO checklist), demo-recording-20260217.mp4 (recording)
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@cerebrohealth.com>

Cc: Cerebro AI Ops <ai-ops@cerebrohealth.com>, procurement@cerebrohealth.com
Date: 2026-02-17T17:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Cerebro performance recap & next-step plan

Thanks Rafael — great summary. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync:

- Latency: we want to be explicit about streaming vs non-streaming. For chat/assist flows (streaming) our target is p95 end-to-end <= 350 ms for typical user messages (~<128 tokens). For batch generation jobs (non-streaming) p95 <= 700 ms for ~1k token outputs is acceptable.
- Throughput: the 600 tokens/sec estimate is fine as a cluster-level sustained baseline, but we care more about peak burst capacity: ability to handle 10k token/sec spikes for short windows (1–5 minutes) without dropping connections.
- Concurrency: target 40 concurrent active sessions is accurate. Additionally, we need session stickiness across a 3-second window to route KV cache effectively.
- Streaming: first-byte < 150 ms is acceptable; delta flush <= 250 ms. The system must support chunked responses and partial-key-value cache warmups.

Procurement contact: procurement@cerebrohealth.com (cc’d).

Security: please send SOC2 Type II and pen-test summary; we will also send a short questionnaire for data retention / transcript access rules.

Next steps from our side: we’ll provide a representative prompt set and a 2-hour traffic profile dump by tomorrow EOD. Once we have the performance checklist signed off I’ll confirm the PO timeline.

Emily
Emily Zhang | Head of AI Platform, Cerebro Health
emily.zhang@cerebrohealth.com | +1 (650) 555-0126
